answer: Each applicant mounts one timber rig over a shale bed, bound to its own key. The rig drills a core in six depths; each depth's target comes from the last reading folded with the key, so a depth opens only after the last reading is filed. At each depth the holder files the pigment of the cuttings before the next unlocks, the final depth locked with a timber brace. A faked reading collapses: no two beds share a strata pattern. One rig costs $340 plus 18 rig-hours; 5,000 phantoms demand 5,000 rigs, $1.7 million and 90,000 rig-hours, because one rig bores one bed and a worn bit never serves twice.
